description:
SIZED s399 (probe-first).  t/base/lex.t, 120 rows, TRANSPILE-FAIL today
(rc 255, zero output).

    Failed to compile s///e expression '"${\<<END}"
    ok $test - heredoc in "" in multiline s///e outside eval
    END

A HEREDOC opened inside `${\ ... }` inside the REPLACEMENT of `s///e`.  The
file mixes it five ways (t/base/lex.t lines 292-326): inside `eval '...'` and
outside, single-line and multiline, and once with `q||` instead of a heredoc.

**THE ISOLATED SHAPE IS A RULE-12 VIOLATION, found while sizing** -- and it is
the more important half of this task:

    my $test = 42;
    $_ = "";
    s|(?:)|"${\<<END}"
    ok $test - heredoc in "" in multiline s///e outside eval
    END
    |e;
    print $_ || "not ok $test\n";

        perl: ok 42 - heredoc in "" in multiline s///e outside eval
        PCL : not ok 42        (rc 0! only a stderr warning)

pl2cl exits 0, prints "Failed to compile s///e expression …" on stderr, and
emits

    (p-=~ $_ (p-subst "(?:)" (lambda () nil) :e))

-- the replacement thunk becomes NIL.  A missing case producing a VALUE the
program then consumes is exactly what rule 12 forbids; it should DIE naming
the expression it could not compile.  (In base/lex.t itself the file DOES die,
rc 255 -- so both behaviours exist depending on which of the five shapes hits
first.  That inconsistency is itself the bug: one input path dies, another
silently substitutes nil.)

SIZE IT AS TWO PIECES:
  1. (Small, do first, independently useful.)  Make the `s///e` replacement
     compiler DIE on a replacement it cannot compile, instead of emitting
     `(lambda () nil)`.  Population: unknown until measured -- run the s399
     GATE-SET scan (scratchpad tools/gate-set-scan.pl, 638 files, ~2.5 min per population)
     grepping for "Failed to compile s///e expression" to see how many files
     silently carry a nil replacement TODAY.  That number is the real finding.
  2. (The feature.)  Make the heredoc inside `${\ }` inside `s///e` compile.
     The heredoc BODY lives on the lines after the statement, so the
     replacement text the s///e compiler is handed is only the first line --
     the terminator and body are elsewhere in the document.  Whatever reads
     the replacement must be handed the heredoc's content the way the ordinary
     interpolation path already gets it (PPI keeps the HereDoc token with its
     content; PCL's StringInterpolation already handles `${\ ... }` and
     heredocs SEPARATELY -- the gap is the two together inside s///e).

Do NOT size the file's 120 rows against piece 2 alone: base/lex.t is a
lexer-torture file (`s/${s|||;\""}not //;` two lines later), so measure what
it scores once it transpiles before promising rows.


PIECE 1 DONE s404 (commit e588c56): _compile_subst_e_expr DIES naming the
replacement it cannot compile, instead of emitting (lambda () nil), and treats
"produced no form" as a failure too.

POPULATION (the task's own ask): a scan of both populations for "Failed to
compile s///e expression" found 7 sites in 2 files — t/op/taint.t (6) and
t/base/lex.t (1) — both of which already fail to transpile for other reasons.
So no verdict moves, which is exactly when to close a rule-12 hole.

DECLINE->DIE BAR (s373, three legs): emission-ab over both populations 657
files 657 SAME / 0 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF; gate-set-scan 638 files 0 changed rows;
sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18516 = baseline, DROPS 12 = 12.  Gate 145/5313.
Guards: 3 rows in Pl/t/regexp-subst-01.t (nonzero exit, the message names the
replacement, no nil thunk in the output).

PIECE 2 (make the heredoc inside ${\ } inside s///e compile) is UNCHANGED and
still the open half of this task.


PIECE 2, PROBED s406 (not started — recording what the failure actually is, so
the next session does not re-derive it).  With piece 1 in place the isolated
shape now DIES loudly, and the message shows the whole replacement text
INCLUDING the heredoc body:

    PCL: cannot compile the s///e replacement '"\${\<<END}"
    ok $test - heredoc in "" in multiline s///e outside eval
    END
    ': Bug. Fell through. Missing case: [ … PPI::Token::Regexp::Substitute s///e … ]

So the replacement text reaching the compiler is COMPLETE.  What goes wrong is
the re-parse: `"\${\<<END}"` is one PPI double-quoted STRING token, so PPI never
sees a heredoc, and the lines that follow (the heredoc BODY and its terminator)
are parsed as CODE.  The body of the op/base/lex.t case contains the text
"multiline s///e outside eval", so PPI lexes an `s///e` token out of the BODY —
which is the "Missing case" above.  The dump is confusing until you notice the
s///e in it comes from the test's own description string.

FIX SHAPE (sized, not endorsed): normalise before parsing — a heredoc pre-pass
on the replacement text that turns `<<ID` / `<<"ID"` / `<<'ID'` / `<<~ID` plus the
following body lines into an inline quoted literal, which is exactly what perl
means by a heredoc in an expression.  THE TRAP: `<<` is also the left-shift
operator, so the pre-pass needs real token context, not a regex on the text —
which is why this is not a drive-by, and why it may be cheaper AFTER Option B
phase 2 owns the term grammar.


PIECE 2 DONE s410 (`1484246`), for the spelling whose heredoc BODY is inside
the s/// delimiters â which is the one the task called the more important half,
the isolated rule-12 shape:

    s|(?:)|"${\<<END}"
    ok $test - heredoc in "" in multiline s///e outside eval
    END
    |e;                             now matches perl exactly

`_splice_interp_heredocs` in Pl/ExprToCL.pm, run ONLY on a replacement that
already failed to compile, so no working shape changes emission.  The body is
HOISTED into a `my` variable rather than spliced in as a literal (the opener
sits inside the `"â¦"`, so a literal ends the string at its own first quote --
measured).  `<<'RAW'` and `<<~END` handled.  Guard rows in
Pl/t/regexp-subst-01.t compare against perl as the oracle.

THE OTHER FOUR SPELLINGS -> task #382: they put the body AFTER the statement,
so it lives in the enclosing DOCUMENT and needs a document-level pre-pass.
All four are inside `eval 'â¦'` and fail into $@ (loud).

t/base/lex.t still does NOT transpile: two lines after the fixed shape it has
`s/${s|||;\""}not //;` (a s/// inside an interpolation block inside a s///
PATTERN) -> "PCL: cannot compile interpolated regex reference". So no row of
its 120 moves yet, exactly as this task's own note warned.
subject: base/lex.t (120 rows): heredoc inside ${\ } inside s///e — SIZED s399, and the isolated shape is a RULE-12 VIOLATION (nil replacement thunk, rc 0)
